mainTopic: Prepaid purchases when prices change (מי שפרע and רבי שמעון), and lending seed wheat to sharecroppers without ריבית
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: the practical difference between two opinions about buying manure in advance is the rainy season. The משנה then allows a buyer to set a price 'at the highest rate', so he gets the best price the market reaches. In a real case, a groom paid in advance for dowry goods for his father-in-law, and the price dropped. רב פפא rules that he pays today's price if he made a 'highest rate' deal, and the original price if he did not. When the רבנן object that money alone does not acquire, רב פפא explains that he only meant to decide who is backing out and so must accept the curse of מי שפרע. רבינא suggests the rule really follows רבי שמעון, who says money acquires. רב פפא answers from a ברייתא that even רבי שמעון does not say money acquires once the price has changed. רב אשי then explains that the groom was a merchant, not a simple שליח. A new משנה allows lending wheat to sharecroppers for seed, to be paid back in wheat, and tells how רבן גמליאל was extra strict with himself. רבא explains that this משנה and a stricter ברייתא reflect places with different customs about who supplies the seed. The amud ends as a new ברייתא begins.

steps.title: The difference between the opinions is the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier question. The difference between the תנא קמא and the רבנן about setting a price for manure is whether you may do it during the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rainy season is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it asked just before this section: what practical difference is there between the two opinions about buying manure in advance?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, you may set a price for manure at any time of year. The רבנן do not allow it during the rainy season, because manure is not commonly available then. So the two opinions only lead to different results in the rainy season.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is between them', meaning this is the practical difference between the two opinions

phrases.english: The rainy season –
is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the תנא קמא and the רבנן, whose argument about buying manure came just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the end of the previous section: what is the practical difference between the two opinions?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference shows up in the rainy season. The תנא קמא allows setting a price for manure then, and the רבנן do not.

steps.title: The משנה: you may set a price at the highest rate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. A buyer may arrange to buy at the best rate the market reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may set a price with him at the highest rate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to begin discussing it. This sets up the story about רב פפא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer pays now for goods he will receive later. He agrees that if the market price drops, he will get the goods at the lowest price of the year. That means he receives the most goods for his money.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets a price, making a deal now for goods to be delivered later
'At the highest rate', meaning the rate that gives the buyer the most goods for his money

steps.confusionAlert: 'Highest rate' does NOT mean the highest price! It means the rate that gives the buyer the most goods per coin. In practice, that is the lowest price.

phrases.english: And he may set a price with him at the highest rate.
phrases.notes: 'Highest' here means the most goods for the money, so the buyer gets the cheapest price the market reaches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer may arrange in advance to receive goods at the best market rate that occurs.

steps.title: רב פפא rules on dowry goods whose price dropped
steps.stepSummary: A man paid in advance for dowry goods, and then the price fell. רב פפא rules: if he set the price 'at the highest rate', he gets the new price; if not, he pays the original price.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man gave money toward a dowry for his father-in-law's household. In the end, the dowry goods got cheaper. They came to רב פפא. He told him: If you set the price at the highest rate, take the goods at today's price. If not, take them at the original price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that uses the משנה's rule. רב פפא decides which price the buyer pays, based on whether he made a 'highest rate' deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer paid early, and then the market dropped. If his deal included 'highest rate', he is entitled to the drop. Without that condition, the original agreed price stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Dowry, the goods a bride brings into the marriage
At the current price / at the original price

phrases.english: There was a certain man who gave money
for the dowry of his father-in-law's household,
in the end the dowry goods became cheaper.
They came before רב פפא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי פְּסַקְתְּ (עִמּוֹ) כְּשַׁעַר הַגָּבוֹהַּ –
phrases.english: He said to him: If you set the price (with him) at the highest rate –
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: take the goods at the current price.
And if not, take them at the original price.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּיהַיב זוּזֵי לִנְדוּנְיָא דְּבֵי חֲמוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's rule of 'highest rate' to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a 'highest rate' agreement, the buyer pays the new lower price. Without it, the buyer pays the original price.

steps.title: The רבנן object: money alone does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רב פפא. If no 'highest rate' deal was made, why must the buyer pay the original price? He only gave money, and money alone does not complete a purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב פפא: If he did not set the price that way, must he take the goods at the original price? It is only money, and money does not acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack the second half of רב פפא's ruling. They argue that the buyer is not locked into the deal at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By rabbinic law, paying money does not complete the purchase of movable goods; the buyer has to physically take them. Since nothing was acquired yet, the buyer should be free to back out. How can רב פפא force him to pay the old price?

keyTerms.meaning: Money does not acquire; paying alone does not finish the purchase of movable goods
The Sages (here, scholars who challenged רב פפא)

phrases.english: The Sages said to רב פפא:
And if he did not set the price that way, must he take the goods at the original price?
It is only money, and money does not acquire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רב פפא's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that without a 'highest rate' deal, the buyer must pay the original price
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money alone does not complete the purchase. So no deal binds the buyer, and he should be free to back out.

steps.title: רב פפא explains: it is about the curse of מי שפרע
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא agrees that money does not acquire. He explains that he only meant that whoever backs out must accept the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I also agree. I was talking about accepting 'מי שפרע'. If he set the price at the highest rate, the seller is the one backing out, so the seller must accept 'מי שפרע'. If he did not, the buyer is the one backing out, so the buyer must accept 'מי שפרע'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He did not mean the buyer is legally forced; he meant that whoever backs out must accept the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Backing out after money was paid is legally allowed. But the person who does it must accept a curse: 'He Who punished the generation of the flood will punish whoever does not keep his word.' רב פפא's ruling only decides who counts as the one backing out. With a 'highest rate' deal, the seller who refuses the low price is backing out. Without one, the buyer who refuses the old price is backing out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He Who exacted payment', a curse given to someone who backs out of a deal after money was paid

steps.whatToRemember: Money alone does not finish a purchase, so either side may still back out. But whoever backs out must accept מי שפרע. A 'highest rate' deal decides who that is when prices drop: the seller if there was such a deal, the buyer if there was not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a deal can carry moral and religious weight even before it is legally binding. The curse of מי שפרע protects people's trust in each other's word.

phrases.english: He said to them: I also agree that money does not acquire;
I was speaking about accepting upon himself 'He Who exacted payment'.
phrases.notes: This is the curse said to someone who backs out after money was paid: 'He Who punished the flood generation will punish whoever does not keep his word.'

phrases.english: If he set the price at the highest rate,
the seller is the one backing out,
so the seller accepts upon himself 'He Who exacted payment'.
If he did not set the price that way –
the buyer is the one backing out,
so the buyer accepts upon himself 'He Who exacted payment'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי לְקַבּוֹלֵי עֲלֵיהּ ״מִי שֶׁפָּרַע״ קָא אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge in step 4 by reinterpreting the ruling in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the ruling decides who receives the curse of מי שפרע, not who is legally forced to complete the sale
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן thought רב פפא was legally forcing the buyer to pay the original price.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither side is forced. The ruling only decides who counts as backing out and so must accept מי שפרע.

steps.title: רבינא asks: maybe this rule follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב פפא how he knows the rule follows the רבנן. Maybe it follows רבי שמעון, who says money acquires. Then for the רבנן, the buyer would always pay the cheaper current price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב פפא: How do you know this rule follows the רבנן, who argue with רבי שמעון and say money does not acquire? You say that even so, if he set the highest rate he pays today's price, and if not, he pays the original price. Maybe the rule follows רבי שמעון, who says money does acquire. That is why, without a 'highest rate' deal, he pays the original price: the money already bought the goods. But for the רבנן, whether or not he set the highest rate, he pays today's price, because a person always has in mind the cheaper price!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the explanation רב פפא just gave. He suggests the 'original price' rule comes from רבי שמעון's view that money acquires. It does not come from the רבנן and the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said the 'original price' rule works even for the רבנן, through the curse of מי שפרע. רבינא says the rule makes more sense for רבי שמעון, because for him the money already locked in the purchase at the old price. For the רבנן nothing was bought yet, so the buyer would simply pay the cheaper current price, since everyone wants the lower rate.

keyTerms.meaning: Money acquires: paying alone finalizes the sale
A person's intention, what he has in mind

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Pappa:
And from where do you know that it is the Rabbis
who disagree with Rabbi Shimon
who say money does not acquire,
and even so:
phrases.notes: He is repeating רב פפא's ruling: even though money does not acquire, the price rule still applies.

phrases.english: if he set the price at the highest rate,
he takes it at the current price,
if he did not set it, he takes it at the original price?
Perhaps it is Rabbi Shimon,
who says money acquires:
and when he set the price at the highest rate,
he takes it at the current price,
if he did not set it, he takes it at the original price,
because the money acquires them.
But according to the Rabbis,
whether he set it or did not set it,
he takes it at the current price,
because a person's mind is set on the cheap price!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב פָּפָּא: וּמִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's explanation in Step 5 that the rule works for the רבנן through מי שפרע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the 'original price' rule follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule fits רבי שמעון (money acquires) better. For the רבנן, the buyer would always pay the cheaper current price, since that is what everyone intends.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי שמעון only means a price that did not change
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי שמעון only says money acquires when the price stayed the same. When the price changed, even רבי שמעון does not say it. Otherwise רבי שמעון would never apply מי שפרע to a buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: Granted that רבי שמעון said money acquires when there is one price. Did he say it when there are two prices? For if you do not say this, then according to רבי שמעון the curse of מי שפרע would never apply to a buyer!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends himself. He limits רבי שמעון's rule to a case where the market price did not change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the price changed, even רבי שמעון agrees the money did not fully lock in the deal. So רבינא's idea that the money acquired at the old price does not work for רבי שמעון either. Proof: if money always fully acquired for רבי שמעון, a buyer could never back out, and the curse of מי שפרע would never apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: One price: the market price did not change
Two prices: the market price changed

phrases.english: He said to him:
Granted that Rabbi Shimon said it
with one price,
did he say it with two prices?
For if you do not say so,
"He Who exacted payment" regarding a buyer,
Rabbi Shimon would not hold of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּחַד תַּרְעָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: רבי שמעון's rule applies only when the price did not change.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא thought that for רבי שמעון money always locks in the old price, even after the price changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the price changed, even רבי שמעון does not say money acquires. So the rule cannot rest on that, and רב פפא's מי שפרע explanation stands.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא that רבי שמעון uses מי שפרע
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say that רבי שמעון really never applies מי שפרע to a buyer. The גמרא rejects this from a ברייתא where רבי שמעון speaks of מי שפרע. So the curse must have a place in his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: yes, that is true, רבי שמעון has no מי שפרע for a buyer. But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'In any case, this is the law, but the חכמים said: He Who exacted payment, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible escape from רב פפא's proof. It brings a ברייתא showing that רבי שמעון does use the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might try to escape רב פפא's proof by accepting that, for רבי שמעון, a buyer never gets מי שפרע. The גמרא answers with a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says 'in any case this is the law, but the Sages said מי שפרע.' The next step shows that the words 'in any case' include the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (bringing up a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe רבי שמעון really never applies מי שפרע to a buyer.

phrases.english: but it was taught:
in any case, this is the law,
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of a statement by רבי שמעון in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: but the Sages said "He Who exacted payment" etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's proof in Step 7 by showing that רבי שמעון does hold of מי שפרע.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does apply the curse of מי שפרע, so money cannot always fully acquire in his view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says: 'in any case, this is the law, but the Sages said מי שפרע'.

steps.title: 'In any case' means the buyer is cursed too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the words 'in any case' in רבי שמעון's ברייתא. They mean that the buyer and the seller alike can fall under the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'in any case' mean? Doesn't it mean that it makes no difference if it is the buyer or the seller? Either one who backs out accepts the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the key words of the ברייתא from Step 8. It shows that רבי שמעון does apply מי שפרע to a buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'in any case' covers both sides of the sale. So רבי שמעון holds that a buyer who backs out can also get the curse. That is exactly what Step 8 needed to show.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He Who exacted payment': the curse given to someone who backs out of a deal after money was paid

phrases.english: What does 'in any case' mean?
Does it not mean that it makes no difference whether it is the buyer
and no difference whether it is the seller:
he accepts upon himself 'He Who exacted payment'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מִכׇּל מָקוֹם? לָאו דְּלָא שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof begun in Step 8 by explaining which words of the ברייתא prove the point.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון applies מי שפרע even to a buyer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'מכל מקום' in רבי שמעון's ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule is only when the price stayed the same
steps.stepSummary: Since a buyer can get מי שפרע in רבי שמעון's view, money cannot always acquire for him. He says money acquires only when there was one price, not when the price changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבי שמעון says money acquires, it is when there was one price. When there were two prices, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the proof. רבי שמעון's rule that money acquires only applies when the price did not change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money always acquired, a buyer who backed out would simply be stuck with the deal, and the curse would never be needed for him. Since רבי שמעון does curse a buyer, there must be a case where money does not acquire, and that case is when the price changed. This backs up רב פפא's answer in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: one price: the price stayed the same

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי שמעון, who says money acquires, agrees that it does not acquire when the price changed. So רבינא's suggestion fails: the 'original price' rule cannot come from money acquiring. It rests on רב פפא's point about who backs out and must accept מי שפרע.

phrases.english: Rather, when רבי שמעון says it,
it is where there is one price;
phrases.notes: 'Two prices' means the market price changed between the time he paid and the time the goods were delivered.

phrases.english: where there are two prices, he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Steps 8 and 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון says money acquires only when the price did not change. When it changed, even he agrees money does not acquire, so רבינא's challenge is answered.

steps.title: Why not just say he was a שליח?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי why רב פפא needed all this reasoning. In רב פפא's case the man was made a שליח from the start, so that alone should explain the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: Let him get the ruling from the fact that the man was made a שליח from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge comes up about רב פפא's ruling. Why not use a simpler reason: the man was acting as a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח is sent to help the one who sent him, not to cause him a loss. Buying at the more expensive price would be against the sender's interest, so the deal should not count for that reason alone. If so, the long discussion about money acquiring seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: let him derive it instead (from a simpler reason)
agent, someone sent to act for another

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
But let him derive it instead
from the fact that he made him an agent from the beginning!
phrases.notes: He means the father-in-law, who sent the groom to buy the dowry goods for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי שמעון question is settled, a new question asks whether a simpler reason would explain רב פפא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning behind רב פפא's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שליח who causes a loss to his sender is not acting as his שליח, so the ruling should come from the rules of שליחות. There seems to be no need to discuss whether money acquires.

steps.title: He was a merchant, not a שליח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the man in the case was a merchant who buys and sells. So the simple שליח argument does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is about a merchant who buys and sells.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the שליח reason does not settle the case. The man was a trader doing business, not simply a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A merchant buys and sells on his own and does not profit on every deal. The father-in-law knows this, so he cannot say 'I sent you only to help me, not to cause me a loss.' That is why רב פפא needed the reasoning about who is backing out and מי שפרע.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is about a merchant who buys and sells.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the man was a merchant, not a simple שליח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man was a שליח, so the deal fails just because he caused his sender a loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was a merchant who trades on his own, so the שליח reason does not apply and רב פפא's reasoning is needed.

steps.title: Lending wheat to sharecroppers for seed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a landowner may lend wheat to his אריסים for planting, to be paid back in wheat, but not for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may lend wheat to his sharecroppers for seed, to be paid back in wheat, but not for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It allows a wheat-for-wheat loan to sharecroppers only when the wheat is for planting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lending wheat and getting wheat back raises a worry of ריבית, since the price of wheat may go up by the time it is repaid. The משנה allows it for seed but not for eating. It does not give the reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: sharecroppers who work the owner's field for a share of the crop
wheat for wheat: a wheat loan paid back in wheat

steps.confusionAlert: This loan is still a ריבית-type case. The משנה gives an exception for seed; it does not say that a wheat-for-wheat loan is never a ריבית concern.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may lend his sharecroppers
wheat for wheat, for seed,
but not to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְוֶה אָדָם אֶת אֲרִיסָיו חִטִּין בְּחִטִּין לְזֶרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wheat-for-wheat loan to sharecroppers is allowed for seed, but not for eating.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל was strict with himself
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells that רבן גמליאל lent wheat for seed to his אריסים and always took it back at the cheaper price. He did this to be strict with himself, not because the הלכה requires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל would lend wheat to his sharecroppers for seed, to be paid back in wheat. Whether he lent when wheat was expensive and the price fell, or when it was cheap and the price rose, he took it back at the cheaper price. This was not because that is the הלכה; he wanted to be strict with himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a story about רבן גמליאל to show that this kind of loan was done. It adds that his extra care was a personal stringency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that a great חכם really lent wheat for seed, which supports the ruling. But he always took the cheaper price, so he never came out ahead. The משנה says clearly that this was beyond the law.

keyTerms.meaning: when it was expensive, and then the price dropped
when it was cheap, and then the price rose

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַלְוֶה אֶת אֲרִיסָיו
phrases.english: For Rabban Gamliel would lend his sharecroppers
wheat for wheat, for seed;
if he lent at a high price and it became cheaper,
or at a low price and it became more expensive,
he would take from them at the cheaper price.
And this was not because that is the halakha,
but because he wanted to be strict with himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַלְוֶה אֶת אֲרִיסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the משנה's ruling with a story and adds that רבן גמליאל's extra care was not required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wheat loan for seed was done in practice. Always taking the cheaper price is only a personal stringency, not the הלכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds a limit: only before the sharecropper went down to the field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the rule of the משנה but limits it. The loan is allowed only if the אריס has not yet gone down to the field; if he already has, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person may lend his sharecroppers wheat for wheat, for seed. When does this apply? When the sharecropper has not yet gone down to the field. But if he has gone down, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא on the same law. The ברייתא adds a condition that the משנה did not mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה allows the seed loan with no conditions. The ברייתא says it is allowed only before the אריס starts working the field. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: in what case was this said?
went down (into the field to start working)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
A person may lend his sharecroppers
wheat for wheat, for seed.
In what case is this said?
When he has not gone down,
phrases.notes: He means the אריס hasn't yet gone down into the field to start working it.

phrases.english: but if he has gone down, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַלְוֶה אָדָם אֶת אֲרִיסָיו חִטִּים בְּחִטִּים לְזֶרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that limits the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seed loan is allowed only before the אריס has gone down to the field; after that it is forbidden.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא make a difference that the משנה does not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה does not distinguish between before and after the אריס went down to the field, while the ברייתא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the תנא of our משנה, who does not distinguish between whether he went down or not? And what is different about the תנא of the ברייתא, who does distinguish between whether he went down or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the משנה and the ברייתא side by side and asks what the difference between them is. This question sets up the explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to allow the seed loan at any time, while the ברייתא forbids it after the אריס went down to the field. The גמרא wants to know what each תנא is thinking. It may be a real dispute, or the two may be talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: the outside תנא, the one of the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is different about the tanna of our mishna,
who does not distinguish
between whether he went down and whether he did not go down,
and what is different about the tanna of the baraita,
who does distinguish
between whether he went down and whether he did not go down?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא תַּנָּא דִּידַן דְּלָא קָא מְפַלֵּיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the ברייתא of Step 15 with the משנה of Step 13 and asks why they differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind each תנא: why the משנה allows the seed loan without conditions, while the ברייתא forbids it after the אריס has gone down to the field.

steps.title: In our משנה's place, the sharecropper normally brings the seed
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רבי אידי, explains that in the place of our משנה the אריס supplies the seed. So until he plants, the owner can still remove him, and the seed-loan is simply part of the work deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי אידי explained it to me. In the place of the תנא of our משנה, the sharecropper gives the seed. So whether he went down to the field or not, as long as he has not put in the seed, the owner can still remove him. When he goes down, he goes down for a smaller share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from step 16. It explains that our משנה was taught in a place where the sharecropper normally brings his own seed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the אריס normally brings the seed, the owner can fire him any time before he plants, even after he has come to the field. So when the owner gives him seed, it is part of the job terms: the אריס accepts a smaller share of the crop to cover it. That makes it a work deal, not a loan, so there is no ריבית problem whether or not he went down.

keyTerms.meaning: the sharecropper, who works the field for a share of the crop
he can remove him, meaning he can still fire him from the job
for less than this, meaning for a smaller share of the crop

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as two sources arguing about the הלכה. Both agree on the rule. They just describe places with different customs about who supplies the seed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, רַבִּי אִידִי אַסְבְּרַהּ נִיהֲלִי:
phrases.english: Rava said: Rabbi Idi explained it to me:
In the place of the tanna of our mishna,
the sharecropper gives the seed,
whether he went down or did not go down,
as long as he has not put in the seed,
the owner can remove him,
and when he goes down,
he goes down for less than this.
phrases.notes: He means the sharecropper agrees to take a smaller share of the crop to cover the seed he got.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, רַבִּי אִידִי אַסְבְּרַהּ נִיהֲלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by setting our משנה in a place with a particular custom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why our משנה does not distinguish between before and after the אריס went down to the field.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In our משנה's place, the אריס supplies the seed, so the owner can remove him until he plants. The seed is therefore always part of a new work deal, at any stage.

steps.title: In the ברייתא's place, the landowner normally supplies the seed
steps.stepSummary: In the place of the ברייתא, the landowner supplies the seed. Before the אריס goes down, the owner can still remove him, so the seed is part of the deal. After he goes down, the owner cannot remove him, so lending the seed is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the place of the תנא of the ברייתא, the landowner gives the seed. If the sharecropper has not gone down yet, the owner can still remove him, so when he goes down he goes down for a smaller share. But if he already went down, the owner can no longer remove him, and the loan is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by explaining the ברייתא's place. Here the custom is the opposite: the landowner supplies the seed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this place, once the אריס has gone down to the field, he is locked into the job and the owner cannot fire him. So the seed can no longer be treated as part of setting new work terms. It becomes a real loan, and getting wheat back for wheat is forbidden as ריבית. Before he goes down, the owner can still change the terms, so it is allowed, just like in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher of the outside teaching, meaning the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה and the ברייתא do not argue. The rule depends on whether the owner can still fire the אריס. If he can, the seed is part of the work deal and it is allowed. If he can't, the seed is a real loan and returning wheat for wheat is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key idea about ריבית: the same handover of wheat can be either a work arrangement or a loan, depending on whether the terms of the job are still open.

phrases.english: In the place of the tanna of the baraita,
the landowner gives the seed,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לֹא יָרַד דְּמָצֵי מְסַלֵּיק לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: if he did not go down, so that the owner can still remove him,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא נָחֵית – לִבְצִיר מֵהָכִי קָא נָחֵית,
phrases.english: when he goes down, he goes down for less than this,

phrases.aramaic: אִי יָרַד דְּלָא מָצֵי מְסַלֵּיק לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: if he went down, so that the owner cannot remove him,
it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַתְרָא דְּתַנָּא בָּרָא, מָרֵי אַרְעָא יָהֵיב בִּיזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by explaining the opposite custom behind the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the ברייתא's place, the owner supplies the seed. Before the אריס goes down, he can be removed, so it is allowed. After he goes down, he cannot be removed, so the seed is a loan and it is forbidden.

steps.title: A new ברייתא begins about what one person may say to another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא with the words "A person may say to his fellow." The rule itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person may say to his fellow:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by starting to quote a new ברייתא. Only the opening words appear here; the actual rule comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words תנו רבנן signal a new teaching from the time of the תנאים. The phrase "a person may say to his fellow" tells us a permitted arrangement between two people is about to be described.

keyTerms.meaning: a person may say to his fellow, which introduces a permitted arrangement

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A person may say to another:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the משנה–ברייתא question, the גמרא opens a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a new ברייתא describing what one person may say to another. The rule itself follows.
